item.title: Data Policy Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 7/30/2026.

The Centre for Information Policy Leadership (CIPL) at Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP is a leading global privacy and data policy think tank working at the intersection of law, policy, and technology with a membership comprising more than 85 multinational companies across a broad range of industry sectors. CIPL's leadership and staff are globally recognized thought leaders in privacy, data, and digital policy, including former senior public and private sector professionals. CIPL is seeking a Data Policy Analyst to join its team in Washington, DC. A J.D. or Master of Public Policy degree is required along with minimum 2 years of relevant work experience.

Key responsibilities include: working closely with CIPL leadership to develop strategies and implement project plans to advance CIPL's global policy agenda on privacy, data, and digital policy issues (including accountable AI, automated decision-making, biometric data, children's data, cross-border data flows, cybersecurity, data-driven innovation, data localization, digital sovereignty, privacy enhancing technologies, and regulatory strategy); monitoring policy trends and developments and summarizing findings to CIPL staff and members in policy readouts, PowerPoint presentations, and reports; conducting research for and drafting regulatory comments, white papers, issue briefs, and articles; planning and delivering virtual and in-person events to socialize CIPL's global policy agenda; managing evolving workloads and deadlines; helping manage collaboration with CIPL member companies, think tanks, academics, industry groups, and policy influencers; helping strengthen relationships with current CIPL members and recruiting new members; and developing materials for CIPL and non-CIPL events, including speaking and representing CIPL at these events.

Qualifications: a J.D. or Master of Public Policy degree (required); minimum 2 years of relevant work experience in-house, at a professional services firm, law firm, think tank, trade association, government, regulatory agency, or legislative staff; excellent knowledge of global privacy, data, and digital laws and policy, and regulation of emerging technologies; strong understanding of the U.S. federal and state legislative/regulatory process; experience writing public consultation responses, white papers, or articles on issues related to data policy; and superb writing, analytical, and communication skills. Additional valued experience includes computer science and/or data analytics, competition law, intellectual property law, regulatory compliance, international trade policy, and knowledge of additional languages.

Compensation and logistics: salary $87,300-$110,000 for Washington, DC (salaries for employees based outside DC may differ). Hunton Andrews Kurth offers a range of benefits and wellness options based on experience, performance, and location. Full-time, Washington, DC office.

item.description:

IMPORTANT: This is a senior leadership role requiring 10 years of experience in performance evaluation or a related field, plus a graduate or professional degree. It is not suitable for early-career candidates.

The Wisconsin Legislative Audit Bureau (LAB) is a nonpartisan service agency that assists the Legislature in maintaining effective oversight of state programs and finances. The Bureau conducts objective audits and evaluations of state agency operations to ensure financial transactions have been made in a legal and proper manner and to determine whether programs are administered effectively, efficiently, and in accordance with the policies of the Legislature and the Governor. The Performance Evaluation Director reports to the State Auditor, represents the Bureau in interactions with senior officials from across state government, and leads the Bureau's performance evaluation function. Based in downtown Madison, WI. Apply by submitting a resume and statement of interest (1-2 pages) to LAB-Employment@legis.wisconsin.gov.

Key responsibilities include: collaborating with other senior leadership and the State Auditor to develop and implement audit plans; managing work of team leaders, establishing expectations, and assessing performance; meeting frequently with evaluation teams to review analyses, plan additional evaluation work, and develop tentative conclusions; performing quality assurance procedures through selected review of documentation; participating in staff development and assisting in recruiting additional staff; effectively balancing staffing resources to meet deadlines; preparing plans to meet requirements of assigned audits; developing appropriate and thorough analyses; monitoring each evaluation to ensure quality and completeness; and preparing timely and accurate evaluation reports.

Qualifications: leadership experience including leading, motivating, and developing staff; ten years of experience in the field of performance evaluation or a related field; knowledge of public policy analysis and methods of measuring program effectiveness and efficiency; demonstrated experience in determining appropriate research strategies, planning and conducting complex performance evaluations, and leading others in performing these functions; critical thinking, analytical, multi-tasking, writing, and oral communication skills; and a graduate or professional degree in an academic discipline emphasizing analytical skills or policy analysis. Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: competitive salary based on relevant professional experience. Comprehensive state benefits package including health insurance, retirement, and paid leave. Based in downtown Madison, WI.

The Wisconsin Legislative Audit Bureau (LAB) is a nonpartisan service agency of the Wisconsin Legislature responsible for conducting performance evaluations and financial audits to ensure public accountability for state resources. The Investigative Auditor staffs the Bureau's Fraud, Waste, and Mismanagement Hotline -- an exciting opportunity for an individual with strong investigative experience. Key responsibilities include: facilitating the process of resolving allegations received through the Hotline; documenting and tracking allegations; obtaining and evaluating information from numerous sources to investigate Hotline allegations; conducting interviews with state agency staff; documenting the investigative process and conclusions for each allegation in accordance with Bureau policies and standards; communicating accurately and concisely the results of each investigation; preparing plans for appropriate investigative steps; investigating multiple issues simultaneously; collaborating and coordinating with other auditors and evaluators; assessing the relevance of information obtained to resolve reported allegations; and efficiently identifying, understanding, and defining the scope of issues in each allegation.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree and five years of professional experience assessing compliance with laws, regulations, and other applicable standards; demonstrated experience with interviewing and investigative techniques, including those involving potential fraud, waste, and abuse; research experience demonstrating the skills to obtain information that is not readily available; and excellent written and verbal communication skills with attention to detail. Preferred: certification as a Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) or Certified Public Accountant (CPA); experience as an auditor; and solid knowledge of state government programs. item.description:
Democracy Forward Foundation is a nonpartisan nonprofit legal organization that litigates and advocates to defend democratic institutions and the rule of law. The Strategic Initiatives team seeks a Research Assistant or Research Analyst to help track and assess the activities of the right-wing legal movement and coordinated efforts to undermine liberal democracy in the United States. The Research Assistant/Analyst will help drive Democracy Forward's research and data collection on right-wing legal organizations, attempts to undermine DEIA policies and practices, and efforts to advance anti-democratic law and policy. The role is hybrid in Washington, DC (8 times per month -- averaging 2 times per week), with remote candidates within the United States also considered (travel to DC expected 1-2 times per quarter). Application deadline: July 23, 2026 at 11:59pm ET. A cover letter describing interest in legal and policy work promoting democracy is required.

Key responsibilities include: supporting efforts to track, analyze, and report on the organization and litigation strategies of the right-wing legal movement and its efforts to undermine democratic institutions and the rule of law; working with policy and research staff to maintain timely, accurate, and robust information about legal and policy trends across a range of progressive issues; collaborating with all teams across the organization to develop useful analyses and synthesis of data on emerging threats to liberal democracy, including litigation trends, personnel networks, and coordinated policy campaigns; staying abreast of current events and the legal and policy landscape related to anti-democratic activities in the United States; preparing briefings for internal staff and external stakeholders; and supporting efforts to collaborate and develop partnerships that enhance Democracy Forward's impact.

Qualifications: for Research Assistant -- 0-2 years of experience working in research, policy, or legal environments; for Research Analyst -- 3+ years of experience in research, policy, or legal environments. All candidates need: demonstrated experience with legal, policy, and media databases and tools including Westlaw, Docket Alarm, PACER, AirTable, Muck Rock, and Google News; experience managing data projects and research functions; excellent writing skills and attention to detail; ability to manage multiple competing deadlines; commitment to democracy and social progress; and strong collaborative and interpersonal skills.

The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission is a legislative branch commission mandated to monitor, investigate, and report to Congress on the national security implications of the bilateral trade and economic relationship between the United States and the People's Republic of China. The Congressional Affairs and Communications Assistant is an early-career opportunity to help influence congressional, media, and broader policy discussions around some of the most consequential issues of the day. Under the direction of the Director of Congressional Affairs and Communications, the position shapes the Commission's engagement with Congress, external stakeholders, and the public through legislative affairs, strategic communications, and outreach efforts. Note: this is a term-appointed position (initial term of one year, generally renewed annually by mutual agreement). Applicants must be eligible for a security clearance (a current active clearance is not a prerequisite). All work must be in-person in Washington, DC. Application deadline: July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT. Apply by emailing a cover letter (addressing specific required points listed in the vacancy announcement), resume, and current writing sample (max 5 pages) in one PDF to Opportunities@uscc.gov.

Key responsibilities include: building and maintaining relationships with Members of Congress and staff; identifying, tracking, and producing a weekly summary of congressional hearings, markups, and legislative actions relevant to the Commission's mandate; contributing to the planning and execution of Commission hearings; drafting briefing materials, talking points, and other congressional engagement products; supporting the development of Commission research products; researching the existing policy landscape to make Commission recommendations concrete and actionable; developing and executing strategic communications and outreach initiatives including podcasts, short-form videos, interviews, panel discussions, and conferences; managing the Commission's digital communications strategy and drafting content across social media, website, newsletters, and promotional materials; assisting in managing the Commission's website; and monitoring media coverage and supporting media relations activities.

Highly desired (not required): experience developing and implementing communications or public affairs strategies; experience managing professional social media accounts and website content management systems; experience pitching or coordinating media interviews, podcasts, or public events; and knowledge of the People's Republic of China and U.S.-China relations.

Compensation and logistics: salary $60,000-$72,000. Full federal employee benefits including health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, FERS retirement, and TSP. Term-appointed (1 year, generally renewed annually). In-person in Washington, DC. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; early submission strongly encouraged.
